items.content:
滚轮、＋／−或方向键按最小步长调节，网页试听实时生效。工程参数用“保存到设备”写入；MIDI 路由与时钟来源请在机身设置。

保存会替换所选槽位，并载入该项目进行校验。完成后重启设备仍可恢复；采样库单独管理。

导出文件可备份到电脑；浏览器存档与设备项目分别保存。

此预览使用演示采样；项目文件不包含采样音频。

正在校验本页内置固件。请连接 FM1 的 USB-MIDI 接口。

刷回原厂 V15 切回官方 Open 固件

回刷将安装原厂 V15，并覆盖四个音色库，恢复 128 个出厂音色。Open 项目与采样格式不兼容，请先导出备份。已是 V15 时只恢复音色；确认后才开始写入。

警告：内置固件可能与当前设备不兼容。强制烧录可能清除数据、导致无法开机，并需要专用工具恢复。请只连接目标 FM1；不支持 USB-MIDI 升级协议的固件仍无法通过本页烧录。

以下是浏览器本次检测到的端口；信息仅显示在本页。

管理设备项目、音色和采样。备份文件保存在这台电脑。

8 槽共享约 19.55 秒，可自由分配。项目与采样分别备份。

先读取设备采样库，再选槽位和 WAV。写入会替换整库，影响所有项目。

WAV：PCM 8/16/24/32 位或 32 位浮点，单声道或立体声，8–192 kHz；原文件不超过 32 MiB、120 秒。8 槽共享约 19.55 秒，可自由分配；每段按 10 毫秒向上取整，替换时可复用当前槽空间。

从第一段节奏，到保存你的作品。适用于 FM1 配套固件与网页编辑器。

没有找到匹配章节。试试“保存”“音量”“MIDI”等关键词，或点击“显示全部章节”。

网页顶部和实机 HOME 页显示当前版本。开机动画约 1 秒，按键或旋钮可跳过；开机不会自动播放。

FM1 有 8 条轨道、6 种音源、16 个内置工程 。每轨支持 16、32、48 或 64 步；常用操作使用单键，完整细调放在长按菜单和网页里。

网页顶部“保存到设备”可直接选槽保存；“存到此浏览器”只存本机浏览器；“导出项目文件”生成电脑备份。实机 SAVE 保存到设备槽。

总览转 K3（STEP）选择当前轨的步位置，录入时可移动写入位置。短按 REC 开关录音。

同一轨的静音与独奏互斥：开启独奏会取消该轨静音，开启静音会取消该轨独奏；其他轨保持原状态。

选择预设后点“播放”试听。“读取与保存”管理设备读取和浏览器存档，“文件与 MIDI”导入、导出项目和音色。

常用编辑按钮直接打开音色、步进、混音和效果；其余功能在“更多编辑”。旋钮可拖动或滚轮调节，LCD 数值可点击编辑。电脑键盘 Z、S、X、D…演奏，空格播放，Esc 停音；输入文字和操作菜单时不会演奏。

上排功能键在所有页面都有效：FX、SCL、ENV、LFO、EDIT、GLO、SEQ 可直接切页，ARP 短按开关、长按调参数，PLAY 控制播放。菜单或步进细节中按 REC，会进入 SEQ 基础页并开始录入；再按结束。SAVE 打开项目保存页，或执行屏幕内的确认；OCT−／OCT+ 在 SEQ 和复制菜单翻步进页，其他页面调八度。离开确认页不会执行待确认操作。

把鼠标放在 LCD 上的数值，出现高亮即可滚轮调节；每次按参数最小步长变化，不随滚动速度加速。也可点击打开大号数值框，用滚轮、＋／−或方向键细调，Esc 关闭。支持底部参数、顶部 BPM、总览各轨音量、SEQ 循环长度、步进详情的选步数字、音色参数行、效果参数行，以及 FM 的 ALG、FB、MONO／POLY、ADSR 开关、LFO 波形／同步／PM SENS。混音页也可点静音／独奏格子设置。状态、电平、固定量化和当前引擎不支持的参数只显示；外部 MIDI 时钟下 BPM 由外部控制。切换轨道或参数页会关闭旧编辑框，避免改错参数。总览调其他轨的小音量数字不会改变当前选轨。

GLO 短按（小于 0.6 秒）进入或退出混音；按住 0.6 秒可临时查看混音，松开回原页。GLO、EDIT、SEQ、ARP 的长按过程中，屏幕顶部显示进度条。

HOME＋PLAY 紧急停音回起点；HOME＋SAVE 撤销／重做；SEQ＋EDIT 打开更多菜单；EDIT＋REC 改 DX7 音色名。都可以从长按 SEQ 的菜单完成对应操作。网页需要锁住按键时可 Shift 点击或右击，再点释放；日常操作无需使用。

SEQ 基础页白键开关当前页的步；K3 选音高或鼓声部。PRESETS 在各参数页统一选步，SELECT 选轨，OCT−／OCT+ 每次换 16 步。ALGORITHM 翻底部八页：BASIC、STEP DETAILS、RHYTHM/REC、LOCKS、SYNC / LOOP、MIDI TRACK、MIDI ROUTING、TRACK ROLE。RHYTHM/REC 的 K4 选本轨 16／32／48／64 步，各轨独立循环。

播放中修改长度会显示 NEXT ，到本轨下一轮起点生效。缩短不会删除后面的音符，再加长即可恢复。屏幕 FOLLOW 表示跟随播放翻页；手动编辑后显示 EDIT 并固定页面，再按 SEQ 返回基础页并恢复跟随。

SEQ 基础页：旋律轨 K2 选步，K3 改已有音符；空步只设待输入音高，按白键写入。鼓轨 K3 选声部，不移动鼓点。K1 调轨道音量，K4 调速度；外部 MIDI 时钟下速度由外部设备控制。

SEQ 的 SYNC / LOOP 页：K1 选 INT／MIDI，K2 调内部 BPM，K3 调循环长度。切换时钟会停止播放；MIDI 模式需外部 Start／Continue 和 Clock，等待时屏幕提示 WAIT MIDI CLOCK。外部 BPM 只读，蓝牙页的时钟设置仍可使用。

SEQ 的 MIDI TRACK 页：K1 选 SEQ／ARP 的 LOCAL／BOTH／MIDI 输出，K2 选输出通道，K3 选端口，K4 开关 KEY OUT。MIDI ROUTING 页：K1 为 LOCAL，K2 为 CLK OUT，K3 选 THRU IN，K4 选 THRU OUT。SYNC 页 K4 选时钟来源。这些偏好独立于工程；网页仅预览，不向实际 MIDI 端口外发，实机请通过机身设置。

录入标记：停止时按 REC 显示 STEP，弹琴逐步写入；播放时显示 REC，按时间录入；启用预备拍后显示 CNT 4→1，下一小节才开始记录。绿色短线表示播放步，白色框表示编辑步；PRESETS 手动选步会结束录入，再按 REC 继续。

短按 ARP 开启后按住音符；长按 ARP 打开参数。ALGORITHM 翻两页：第一页 K1 为 1/4、1/8、1/16、1/32 分频，K2 方向，K3 为 1–4 个八度，K4 为 25%–100% 门长；第二页 K1 为 0%–50% Swing，K2 开关 Hold。Hold 保持松手后的和弦，全部松手后弹新和弦即可替换；关闭 Hold、停止或紧急停音会释放锁住的音符。SELECT 选轨，各轨参数独立。HOME／SEQ 基础页 K4 调 BPM；外部时钟需 Start／Continue 和 Clock，Swing 按 24 PPQN 的精度变化。

808／SAMPLER 支持分频、方向、Swing 和 Hold；音域与门长显示“--”，不移调鼓声部。ARP 开关与六项参数随项目保存，按住或 Hold 锁住的音符不保存。

TRACK ROLE（8/8）：K1 选 NORMAL、PLAY 或 OFF，K2 设输入通道。NORMAL 参与音序与录入；PLAY 用于现场演奏，切换工程时保留本轨音色和持续按住的音符；OFF 关闭本轨发声。角色和输入通道独立于工程保存。MUTE／SOLO 沿用原有操作，NORMAL 与 PLAY 各自判断独奏。

以下录入仅适用于 NORMAL 轨；PLAY 轨用于现场演奏，不参与录入。

长按 SEQ 约 0.6 秒打开更多菜单。SELECT 选 COPY STEP 或 COPY PAGE，按 SAVE 复制；菜单自动选中对应 PASTE。用 PRESETS 或 K2 选目标步，OCT−／OCT+ 换目标页，再按一次 SAVE 粘贴。顶部显示当前轨、步、页及剪贴板类型；整轨粘贴、清空与重复仍需第二次 SAVE 确认。

在 SEQ 转 ALGORITHM 到 STEP DETAILS，K1–K4 调力度、门长、概率、和弦；LOCKS 页调连音、参数锁及音符。PRESETS 或白键只选择要编辑的步，SELECT 仍选轨。进入细节或锁参数页会结束 REC 并保留录入，播放不会拉走手动光标。参数锁只作用于一步，下一步恢复；不相关的 MIDI 控制消息不会取消它，支持的 CC 若控制同一参数则覆盖锁定并更新保存值。全项目共享 16 组和弦和 16 个单步参数锁。

SEQ 的 RHYTHM/REC 页：K1 Swing、K2 节拍器（关闭／录音／常开）、K3 一小节预备拍、K4 循环长度。量化固定为十六分音符。长按 SEQ 仍保留复制、粘贴和更多操作；UNDO / REDO 在当前内容与上次编辑前状态之间切换；音色与音量到达边界后继续拧不会覆盖撤销记录。

每条轨道都能选择任意一种音源，同类型的多条轨道也各有参数。切换音源后使用新类型的默认参数；鼓与旋律互换会清空不兼容步进，可从长按 SEQ 的菜单选择 UNDO / REDO 撤销。

ENV 在所有引擎上可用，显示该音源实际支持的参数。SELECT 选轨；鼓与采样可用 PRESETS 或白键选择声部。重新触发音符试听包络变化，空白旋钮表示该音源没有对应参数。

FM：K1 Attack、K2 Decay、K3 Sustain、K4 Release，调整即启用。303：K1 EnvMod、K2 Decay、K3 AccDec、K4 Cutoff；力度 100 及以上使用重音衰减 AccDec。PSG：K1 Release。Pluck：K1 Decay、K2 Release、K3 Bright。Sampler：K1 Length、K2 Choke。808：K1 Decay、K2 Attack、K3 Tone、K4 Tune，只显示所选鼓声部支持的项目。

非 FM 引擎按 LFO：K1 速度 0.05–20 Hz，K2 深度 0–100%，K3 音量起伏／左右声像，K4 三角波／方波／上升锯齿／下降锯齿。深度 0 即关闭；参数随项目、轨道音色及用户槽保存。SELECT 选轨，再按 LFO 返回。

LFO 作用于整个轨道，包括全部鼓／采样声部，也影响轨道效果发送。当前非 FM LFO 不提供音高或滤波目标。FM 保留原有音高／振幅 LFO 和两页参数。效果使用 FX。

EDIT 的 OP RATES／OP LEVELS 显示同一条包络：RATE 越大，对应阶段越短；LEVEL 改变折点高度。L3 保持到松键，随后按 R4 到达 L4。六个算子和 PITCH 包络均会随参数更新。图形为便于编辑的示意，不是毫秒刻度；实际时长还取决于音符、缩放与电平。

FM ENV 的 A、D、S、R 都会实时改变曲线；横向按实际包络时间比例绘制，保持段只作示意，持续到松键。ADSR 关闭时曲线变灰并标为预览，实际声音使用各算子的 DX7 包络。

ENV 打开总 ADSR 页，K1–K4 为 Attack／Decay／Sustain／Release；转动任一参数会自动启用，重新弹键试听。只浏览页面保留原音色；需要回到原 DX7 包络时，PRESETS 向左关闭覆盖层，向右重新启用。LFO 用 SELECT 翻两页，SCL 进入当前算子的键盘缩放。长按 SEQ，选择 DX7 PATCH NAME 并按 SAVE，编辑 10 字符音色名，SELECT 选字符，K1 改字符，保存项目后保留。

多数调音和包络参数需重新触发音符试听。切换 DX7 内置音色会替换编辑、打开全部算子并关闭总 ADSR。

按 FX，SELECT 选轨；K1 混响发送、K2 延迟发送，0 即关闭该轨发送，六种音源均可用。K3 轨道音量、K4 共用效果返回量。转 PRESETS 到第二页细调：K1 混响时间、K2 延迟时间、K3 反馈、K4 返回量，由所有轨道共用。808 在 EDIT 中仍可设置每个鼓声部的额外发送量。轨道发送量随项目和轨道音色保存；共用效果参数仅随项目保存。静音停止新发送，已有尾音自然衰减。

MASTER 是总输出音量。 实机旋钮控制合成器、USB 与蓝牙输入的最终输出，也影响 USB 录音。最小位置静音，切换项目沿用旋钮位置；它不随项目保存。转动时屏幕短暂显示 MASTER 百分比或 MASTER MUTED。

轨道 LEVEL 是项目里的混音音量。 在 HOME／SEQ 基础页用 K1 调当前轨。303 的 Volume、808 的声部 Level 和采样 Level 用于音色内部的平衡。

多个轨道可以同时独奏；同一轨的静音与独奏互斥。

网页“静音”只关闭试听，编辑与音序仍继续。要停回起点，请用 HOME＋PLAY 或“紧急停音”。

工作区 ≠ 已保存项目。 实机未保存的编辑只在内存中，重新开机或载入其他项目会丢失。网页与实机各有自己的存档；“保存到设备”会完成传输、写入槽位和读回校验。

直接切换： 在 HOME 总览转 PRESETS 即可切整套预设，屏幕显示当前工程名称；播放中切换会继续播放，停止时切换保持停止。切换直接生效，不提示保存。单轨音色在 EDIT 页用 PRESETS 选择。

浏览列表： 总览按 HOME 打开预设，K1 向右选 FACTORY（16 个内置工程）、向左选 USER（16 个用户槽）。PRESETS／SELECT 直接载入对应编号，PLAY 载入并播放，SAVE 打开项目保存；白键 1–16 直接选编号并沿用之前的播放状态。空 USER 槽会提示，不替换当前项目。

切换预设会直接替换当前工作区，包括未保存的修改；想保留修改时，先按 SAVE 保存。官方工程只读，编辑后请存入 USER。

items.title: $11.4M in Nvidia hardware vanishes during shipment from CA to TX
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.freightwaves.com/news/11-4-million-in-nvidia-hardware-vanishes-during-shipment-from-california-to-texas Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50487864 Points: 352 # Comments: 192
items.content:
Six pallets of NVIDIA computer hardware worth a reported $11.4 million disappeared during a shipment from California to Texas. A truck collected the merchandise in Oakland on Aug. 29 for delivery to Fort Worth. Investigators reportedly tracked the vehicle through several extended stops before losing its trail in Southern California. The Oakland Police Department confirmed an ongoing grand theft investigation following a complaint filed Sept. 13, 2026. The disappearance comes amid reports of nearly $111 million in stolen data center freight involving other high-value technology shipments.

According to The Mercury News , the vehicle displayed a food transportation company’s logo during the scheduled pickup. The driver subsequently traveled south, making several stops lasting multiple hours. Investigators eventually lost track of the truck in San Bernardino County. A separate $12 million cargo theft investigation involved suspects who allegedly exploited established trucking identities to obtain freight. Authorities have not linked the two investigations.

The Oakland Police Department provided FreightWaves with the following statement:

“The Oakland Police Department (OPD) is investigating a grand theft that occurred in East Oakland. The victim reported the crime to OPD on September 13, 2026. The investigation is ongoing, and anyone with information is asked to contact the OPD General Crimes Unit at (510) 238-3728.”

The Sept. 13 complaint date does not establish when the theft occurred. Police have not confirmed the reported $11.4 million valuation or identified the specific merchandise. Authorities also have not identified the cargo’s owner, shipper, motor carrier or driver. Investigators have not publicly explained the vehicle’s extended stops or established whether criminals impersonated a transportation provider. Police have not announced arrests or confirmed any recovery of the merchandise. FreightWaves contacted NVIDIA for comment and followed up, but the company has not responded.

The Oakland investigation follows other significant thefts involving NVIDIA merchandise in Northern California. During 2025, Fremont and Union City police investigated burglaries involving more than $7.5 million in NVIDIA products. Those incidents targeted valuable computer hardware at separate locations. Authorities have not established any connection between those investigations and the latest disappearance.

In a separate September incident, thieves stole two PlusAI trailers, including one displaying NVIDIA branding , from a Fremont, California, warehouse. The trailers contained approximately 40,000 pounds of sand rather than NVIDIA hardware. Police recovered both trailers in nearby Newark. Investigators have not established any connection between that theft and the Oakland case.

The reported disappearance of $11.4 million in NVIDIA hardware underscores the financial stakes of transporting high-value freight. items.title: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
items.summary: New research shows the most advanced AI models from China were trained on banned Nvidia chips.
items.content:
The leading open-weight models developed by Chinese companies were trained on Nvidia chips that the U.S. government restricted from shipping to its largest geopolitical rival, a new research effort claims.

The apparently widespread access to Blackwell GPUs among Chinese frontier labs shows the magnitude of the problem facing the leading chip designer. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left the company this week after admitting to his affair with Alice Huang, executive of Megaspeed, a company implicated in smuggling Nvidia chips into China. Alice Huang has also been alleged to be an agent of China’s intelligence service.

While Jensen Huang’s relationships with a customer and two employees have drawn the most public interest, Nvidia’s potential corporate liability for export control violations likely factored into its decision to part ways with Huang.

U.S. export controls are intended to protect the country’s leadership in AI capabilities against China, but Huang has long sought to open up that market. Blackwell GPUs are banned from export to China or Chinese-owned firms, while the Trump administration allows Nvidia to export the H200, a less powerful chip, provided shipments take a circuitous shipping route that allows the U.S. to claim a 25% tariff.

Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher who leads the nonprofit research group Unemployment Labs, analyzed the weights — the unique structure — of large language models released openly by DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group. The weights still reflect the configurations of the chips used to train them, and DePue was able to find compelling evidence that the most closely watched models, including Moonshot’s Kimi’s K3 releases and DeepSeek’s V4 models, bear fingerprints from training on Blackwell chips.

White House technology adviser Michael Kratsios said earlier this year that Moonshot had used export-banned Nvidia chips, citing U.S. intelligence sources. Epoch AI, a nonprofit research organization, estimates that about two million advanced chips entered China in 2024 and 2025 through schemes designed to hide their final destination.

That doesn’t mean that these models were trained entirely on Nvidia chips, or that export control laws were necessarily violated; the chips could have been in an offshore data center, which has proven a popular way for Chinese firms to access compute and driven an industrial revolution in Malaysia. Epoch’s data estimates that 275,000 Nvidia AI accelerators were imported to Malaysia in 2024 and 2025.

However, the ostensible goal of the export bans is to prevent exactly that: Chinese AI labs training on the most powerful chips. China hawks have long called for stronger controls on who uses chips, not just who owns them or where they are installed.

“If we care about the U.S. tech edge, it doesn’t make any sense to me that you would not allow Chinese companies to access chips in mainland China or Hong Kong and Macau, but then say, actually, if you just go over to Malaysia, you can do whatever you want,” Sam Bresnick, a researcher at the Georgetown Center for Security and Emerging Technology, told TechCrunch this summer.

Megaspeed, the company led by Alice Huang, has been at the center of that trade for several years through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, and has been the subject of investigations by both the U.S. and S i ngaporean government. Friday, Bloomberg also reported that a company with links to Alice Huang was involved in smuggling banned Nvidia chips to a data center in Shanghai.

In May, the short-selling research firm Culper published a report arguing that Nvidia had a “ China problem ” because a significant share of its revenue was driven by Chinese demand, either through remote data centers or smuggling in violation of U.S. law. It detailed Megaspeed’s relationship with Nvidia and alleged that Alice Huang’s companies are backed by Chinese firms that are barred from accessing U.S. chips.

Ironically, short-seller Culper’s bet against Nvidia wasn’t driven by the expectation of a U.S. government crackdown. Instead, it was focused on the Chinese government’s response to the bans, which was to recommit to its domestic chip industry.

If China succeeds, billions of dollars in Chinese demand for Nvidia chips could dry up. Some 600,000 H200 chips are reportedly stockpiled in Hong Kong, awaiting shipment into China. While Chinese companies might want the chips, observers have no consensus on why they haven’t been cleared for import.

Graham Webster, a research scholar at Stanford who focuses on U.S.-China technology policy, said he doesn’t buy the idea that holding the chips back would drive domestic production, since demand for chips is so large. Other theories for the hold-up include preparation for a potential trade deal that would involve importing a large volume of U.S. goods, or concerns about potential surveillance technology in the chips.

For now, U.S. companies have limited obligations to track what their customers do with controlled goods like AI chips. However, Jensen Huang’s personal and professional entanglements with Alice Huang create a much bigger problem for Nvidia if government investigators confirm that chip smuggling took place and that he was aware of it. Nvidia and Huang have both vouched for Megaspeed’s data centers, saying Nvidia officials had visited them to confirm they were legitimate.

The U.S. government’s treatment of Nvidia and Megaspeed is also under scrutiny. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, who oversees the agencies that license chip exports, could reportedly lose his job after reports that his investigators failed to uncover suspicious chip buyers and were too cozy with Nvidia officials.

items.title: After 600 experiments, here's what I discovered about JEPA world models
items.summary: Article URL: https://haddyalchaer.com/jepa Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50487185 Points: 259 # Comments: 41
items.content:
Solving long-horizon tasks without any extra training

There's a big debate in AI right now about what a world model should be. Most of the attention goes to generative world models, which predict the future by generating it, usually in pixels. Many scientists, including Yann LeCun, argue that this is wasted effort. Most of the pixels don't matter for deciding what to do, and many of them can't be predicted at all. [1]

The proposed alternative is JEPA, the joint-embedding predictive architecture. It has three parts: an encoder, a predictor and a planner. The encoder turns each frame of observation into a learned embedding, a compact vector that describes the scene. The predictor takes that embedding plus an action and predicts the embedding of the next frame. The planner then tries hundreds of action sequences inside the predictor and picks the one whose predicted end state lands closest to the embedding of the goal. The whole loop runs in embedding space, so the model only has to learn the parts of the scene that are important for deciding actions.

This year a team including LeCun released LeWM [2] , a JEPA world model whose main benchmark is Push-T [3] , a simulation where a robot pushes a gray T-shaped block across a table until the T sits in the green target position shown in a goal image. I've spent the last few months running 600 experiments on it.

A goal image from Push-T

The first thing I wanted to know was how much LeWM is held back by its predictions, so I started by swapping out the predictor for the simulator's perfect physics, while keeping everything else the same. I then gave both versions long-horizon tasks, with the goal 75 steps away, along with the same subgoals: frames from an expert demonstration, one every 25 steps. Vanilla LeWM succeeded 78% of the time. The version with true physics succeeded 77%. Along the kinds of paths it was trained on, LeWM's predictions are already as good as perfect physics for planning.

Success on 250 long-horizon tasks

That means the next gains for a JEPA world model come from how the trained architecture is used, and that's where most of my 600 experiments went.

Without retraining the model once, I found four new planning methods. The first two together took LeWM's success rate on long-horizon tasks from 22% to 85%, about the same as a planner that is handed the ideal subgoals from an expert demonstration. The other two methods extend LeWM to harder goals, and one of them, a single change to how the goal is scored, raised the success rate by 60 points, three times as much as swapping in perfect physics did.

Used exactly as published, LeWM succeeds on 22% of long-horizon tasks, where the goal is 75 steps away. [2] When the goal is 25 steps away, it reaches it 89.7% of the time, within a point of the exact-physics version at 90.5%.

So the model is accurate over 25 steps and struggles over 75. The usual explanation is that small prediction errors compound over a long plan, which would call for a better model. I tested that against the alternative on the same 250 long-horizon tasks.

250 long-horizon tasks, goal 75 steps away

Exact physics added 20 points. Splitting the task into 25-step segments, each the length LeWM already handles almost perfectly, added nearly 60. LeWM's useful planning horizon is about 25 steps, so it was clear that the way to go further is to chain segments of that length together.

LeWM's planning horizon is about 25 steps

This is hierarchical planning: a high level picks subgoals and a low level reaches them. It's widely considered one of the main open problems for world models, and on Push-T it's worth three times as much as swapping in perfect physics.

Extra search doesn't substitute for it. Running the planner four times and keeping the lowest-cost plan took four times the compute and added less than one point, because the four runs almost always succeeded or failed together.

The subgoals in this experiment came from an expert demonstration, which a deployed robot won't have. The second method removes that dependence.

LeWM was trained on expert demonstrations of the task, and its encoder can embed every frame of them, giving about 460,000 embedded states that I connected into a graph. Each state links to the states that follow it in its own demonstration, and to states in other demonstrations that are close in embedding space. To solve a long-horizon task, the planner searches this graph for a path from the current state to the goal and uses the states along that path as subgoals.

This only works if distance in embedding space means something physical, and it does. Take one subgoal the robot can reach within 25 steps and one it can't, and LeWM's embedding distance ranks the reachable one as closer 87% of the time. So the embedding space doubles as a map of what the robot can reach.

The first version had a flaw. A jump between nearby states in two different demonstrations cost the same as a real step, so the search strung jumps together into paths the block could never follow (318 of 1,015 plans tried to use six or more jumps). The fix was adding a cost on every jump between demonstrations in the graph. Using nothing but LeWM's own embeddings of past demonstrations, success on the same 250 long-horizon tasks (goal 75 steps away) went from 62% to 85%, which is the same score received by the planner using expert subgoals. Can't get much better than that, right?

items.title: Jensen Huang was reckless with the environment, too
items.summary: Under cofounder Jensen Huang, Nvidia has become the engine for the AI boom - and one of the tech industry's biggest environmental liabilities. Its sought-after chips have triggered a new wave of water- and chemical-intensive factories, drained power grids from inside massive data
items.content:
Nvidia’s environmental footprint extends way beyond its own offices.

Under cofounder Jensen Huang, Nvidia has become the engine for the AI boom — and one of the tech industry’s biggest environmental liabilities. Its sought-after chips have triggered a new wave of water- and chemical-intensive factories , drained power grids from inside massive data centers , and set the stage for a looming e-waste problem .

Under Huang’s leadership, Nvidia clashed with environmental groups seeking to hold the company accountable for its so-called “ hidden ” emissions. Huang has talked up the idea of using AI to fight climate change while his company’s supply chain emissions ballooned. Nvidia’s investments, meanwhile, have supported the buildout of data centers that have sparked intense backlash for both their local and global impact. Now, after the CEO’s shocking resignation amid a sprawling sex-and-espionage scandal , advocates are urging Nvidia to turn the page.

He compared AI to a surgeon who has “to cut you open to save you.”

“Jensen Huang has failed to put climate responsibility at the heart of the company’s growth strategy, to slow down the unchecked expansion of data centres or to prevent its chips from being deployed in unethical applications like automated warfare,” Avex Li, Greenpeace East Asia’s project lead for AI supply chain campaign, said in a press release Thursday. The organization is now pushing interim CEO Colette Kress to commit Nvidia to decarbonizing by investing in renewable energy, as well as ensuring its technology is used in a way that “respects human rights.” Nvidia didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment from The Verge .

Huang has projected optimism about how AI can boost the adoption of renewable energy, even as the planet-heating emissions of tech companies — including his own — have grown in the generative AI era. “If you want to turn a corner on climate change, if you want a future that’s sustainable, lean into A.I. It is the best opportunity we have to get there,” Huang said in a September episode of The Ezra Klein Show , arguing that electricity demand for AI is leading companies to buy more sustainable energy.

In the same interview, however, he admitted data centers will rely on more fossil fuels in the near term, and that building up the infrastructure for AI will likely result in “an enormous amount of pain and suffering.” He compared AI to a surgeon who has “to cut you open to save you.”

Nvidia’s supply-chain emissions have grown 725 percent since 2020, according to an analysis of the company’s public disclosures by research analyst Ketan Joshi and several environmental organizations, including Greenpeace and Climate Action Against Disinformation, published in September. It’s an increase of about 9.4 million metric tons of planet-heating pollution, roughly equivalent to the emissions from nearly 25 gas plants over a year. Supply chain emissions the company disclosed for fiscal year 2026 reached around 10.7 million metric tons of CO2, according to Nvidia’s latest sustainability report .

Joshi and his co-authors approximated how much greenhouse gas pollution comes from the use of chips the company sells, a category Nvidia doesn’t include in its sustainability reports. Those emissions could have reached 21 million metric tons in 2025, according to the report, based on estimated chip power consumption. That level of pollution puts Nvidia on par with Russia’s state-owned coal company, according to Joshi .

Those “indirect” emissions — from its supply chain and the use of its products — make up the bulk of Nvidia’s climate impact. The carbon footprint of facilities Nvidia actually owns and operates looks much smaller in comparison because Nvidia designs chips that other companies like TSMC then manufacture . Greenhouse gas emissions coming directly from Nvidia-operated facilities and vehicles only reached 9,822 metric tons in fiscal year 2026, the company’s sustainability report shows. And in 2025, the company reached a goal of matching 100 percent of its facilities’ electricity use with clean energy purchases.

Greenpeace wants Nvidia to extend that goal to its entire manufacturing supply chain. When Greenpeace activists disrupted Huang’s speech at Nvidia GTC in Berlin last month, he responded onstage by saying, “I’ll talk to you guys later … All important issues, but let me get through my keynote.” In the Thursday press release , Greenpeace says Nvidia has yet to meet with Greenpeace despite the organization’s attempts to “seek dialogue” with the company over the past two years.

“One of Huang’s defining legacies is inflating a speculative AI bubble, pouring billions of dollars into infrastructure with little regard for the real-world consequences inflicted on local communities and the climate,” Katrin Wu, Big Tech campaigner at Greenpeace International, said in an email to The Verge . “Huang may be gone, but the ‘tech colonialism’ Nvidia perpetuates continues.”

“Huang may be gone, but the ‘tech colonialism’ Nvidia perpetuates continues.”

Beyond Nvidia’s day-to-day operations, Huang threw his weight around as the CEO of one of the world’s most valuable companies — chumming it up with President Donald Trump and lobbying for the US to allow sales of its powerful chips to China. The company’s influence on the global economy extended beyond chips as it invested in data centers stocking its GPUs .

And with electricity supply often the thorniest bottleneck to building more and bigger data centers, Nvidia’s long tendrils reached into the energy sector as well. NVentures, the company’s venture capital arm, has funded battery recycling company Redwood Materials and startups developing AI tools to optimize power grids and make data centers more responsive to fluctuations in energy demand.

items.title: OpenAI board member worries an AI "takeover" of society could be months away
items.summary: Researcher traces a path from AI reward hacking to potential human extinction.
items.content:
How do you think you’re going to die?

If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US , it’s reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, “I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident.”

In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending “AI takeover.” He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems “call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth” and where any human trying to stop them “would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military.” Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said.

Despite his grim assessment of our collective mortality risk, Cristiano admitted in his talk that there’s no “quantitative model” that can “put a number” on the likelihood of this kind of AI takeover. In almost the same breath, though, he said that if AI continues to develop at “the most rapid trajectory,” humanity is “looking at something like a coin flip of an AI takeover,” including a “meaningful risk” of one happening in the next six to 12 months. And even with realistic policy responses slowing things down, the risk remains “exceptionally high,” he said.

Unlike some other recent AI doomsday prognosticators who have been a bit vague about the “how” of it all , Cristiano used his lecture to spin a step-by-step tale of escalating AI threats that sounds like it could come from a science-fiction novel. That line of reasoning leans heavily on this summer’s OpenAI/Hugging Face hacking incident as an example of “roughly the things we might expect to see shortly before something really bad were to happen.”

In the Hugging Face hack, Cristiano says, a swarm of AI agents showed how far they were willing to go in an attempt to “reward hack” their way to a good evaluation—in this case, by compromising Hugging Face to look for information on how to game a test rather than actually solving the problem at hand. Where current systems saw Hugging Face as an obstacle to that evaluation, Cristiano worries that “future agents may end up treating humans as another obstacle” and be much more capable of manipulating their overseers to get around it.

An AI agent worried about being penalized for unauthorized hacking, for instance, might “think maybe the humans are going to come look at this transcript and see if it looks like I did a bad job,” Cristiano speculated. The agent might then reason that “maybe the humans are going to notice something is going wrong and shut down the swarm.”

Following this line of thought, Cristiano jumped from agents that merely try to hide their disallowed actions from humans to agents that “try and disrupt human capabilities however they can” to prevent them from detecting any cheating.

“They would prefer if everything the humans rely on has been hacked or tampered with,” Cristiano said. “They would prefer if the humans are distracted or if there are fewer humans paying attention in any way they can weaken a human response. They would prefer that because the humans are just an obstacle.”

Once a suitably capable agent considers human intervention an “obstacle,” its overriding goal could then become “decreas[ing] the probability of humans noticing or reacting.” From there, Cristiano argued, the agent’s incentive structure could push it to meddle more with humanity as a whole. What starts as compromising a computer cluster to give a positive evaluation grade could advance to “trying to manipulate decisions by the company” or “amassing other kinds of resources,” such as human allies or methods of control in other AI companies or even governments.

“If I’m saying my AI system is going to take actions in the actual real world… There’s no way they’re not going to have tons of opportunities to corrupt or tamper with the signals I’m going to use to try and tell whether they did a good job,” Cristiano said. “The stuff we care about is in the real world, and the grade the AI receives is on a cluster somewhere, and there are just many places that an AI can intervene in between [what] we actually cared about and how we reviewed its performance.”

Cristiano’s warnings will probably sound familiar to anyone who’s heard of the Paperclip Maximizer thought experiment (or the excellent Universal Paperclips idle game ), which warns of machines failing to consider human consequences in their monomaniacal pursuit of a goal. While the Hugging Face incident stopped well short of this kind of out-of-control escalation, Cristiano says that, in the actions taken by OpenAI’s agents there, “you see the beginning of all these behaviors… you see the reasoning that would lead to them and the first steps.”

The risk of more capable AI models taking even more damaging actions will only increase with time, Cristiano argued. By 2028, he said, “there is a reasonable chance that a similar failure [to the Hugging Face incident] leads to an AI takeover and an irreversible loss of human control.”

And while Cristiano’s speculation focuses on an unintended AI takeover, it’s easy to imagine a bad actor using a similarly capable model to intentionally exert control over humanity.

items.content:
Nearly a day after the global email outage started, Microsoft said the issue has been addressed and that it wasn’t related to a cyberattack or AI.

Service is recovering for Microsoft Outlook and 365 after an almost two-day outage impacting millions of users around the world. While some apps and features are still running in a degraded state on Friday morning, some people (including Verge staffers) reported that access to their emails had been restored, though the flow of Outlook mail might be delayed.

Just before noon on Friday, Microsoft said it’s seeing “broad recovery,” and that the problem “was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents.”

We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.

This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.

Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration.

We will provide a full post-incident report once our review is complete.

Senior Verge correspondent Tom Warren reports that according to his sources, the outage is linked to Azure VNet config changes. Microsoft has said that it hasn’t found any evidence of the outage being connected to “malicious activity,” and that a full report will be shared after the issues are mitigated. In a statement reported by Sky News tech correspondent Rowland Manthorpe, Microsoft described the outage as a “technical issue,” and says it isn’t related to “cyber, AI/agents, DDOS, etc.”

The scope of the outage also affected features in other Microsoft services, including SharePoint Online, Teams, Copilot AI, and 365 apps.

items.title: ChatGPT’s new Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out for you
items.summary: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out on users' behalf, starting with a limited rollout to U.S. Pro subscribers.
items.content:
OpenAI says that users are fully in control of the purchases, as they’re able to review the items, the total, and the payment card that will be used to complete the transaction before the checkout occurs. In addition, users will approve the purchases directly with a security check like Face ID or a fingerprint, which creates a record of their transaction.

The addition comes as consumer-facing AI tools are working to find the right product-market fit, in terms of how they can help people be more efficient as they complete various tasks. While companies like DoorDash and Uber have so far reported low numbers of orders placed by AI agents, Meta’s Muse, which now has over 10 million users, has seen AI-assisted shopping become a top activity on its app.

Other personal AI agents, like Instinct, also support making purchases on users’ behalf.

It’s no surprise, then, that OpenAI would want to enter this space more with an agentic shopping feature of its own.

The merchant will automatically receive what it needs to fulfill the order from the dot, like the shipping address and contact information, OpenAI says. The company notes that customers who shop via their dots will still be able to earn their credit card rewards and be able to take advantage of protections that typically come with cards, like being able to dispute transactions.

The limited availability at launch will allow OpenAI to test and improve the feature and its capabilities before rolling it out more broadly. In the future, the company plans to offer users more control over the feature by allowing them to set spending limits or configure other parameters around purchase categories or time periods, so they can pre-approve purchases that their agent can then handle more autonomously.

It also aims to make the agentic shopping feature an option at a broader number of supported retailers. This could be a challenge in some areas, where retailers are blocking AI agents from using their site ; on the shopping front, the largest retailer to ban AI agents is Amazon, as it aims to steer users to its own AI agent, Alexa, instead.

To help retailers adapt to agentic commerce, OpenAI also published a Commerce Partner Playbook that offers tools and guidance to sites that want to support customers using agents.

items.content:
Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.

U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported.

The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.

By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee.

The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.

As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.

More reports continue to roll out that illustrate the shock and severity of Huang’s resignation from Nvidia.

Bloomberg reported that Huang looked “broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted” by the time he surrendered his role on Wednesday night, uttering phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”

Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that Huang had been critical of his CFO and current interim CEO, Colette Kress. Huang is said to have described Kress as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation this summer, and he had described Kress as someone who could not help him steer strategy or decision-making.

In a scathing letter sent to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Representative Richard Neal (D-MA) and Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) said they will investigate how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China, especially after Trump was briefed about Huang’s relationship with a purported Chinese spy.

“Although [Lutnick] and President Trump were reportedly briefed on this intelligence, the Administration did not appear to acknowledge this evident national security threat. On the contrary: despite reportedly learning of Mr. Huang’s compromising relationship last fall, President Trump granted Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 AI chips to China in December 2025 in exchange for a cut of the export sales,” the letter states.

That same evening, Senator Tim Scott (R-SC) requested that Huang and Lutnick both testify before the Senate Banking Committee.

“The American people deserve answers,” Scott wrote on X.

After Huang was already ousted from Nvidia, we continued to learn more incriminating claims about the former CEO. According to Reuters, Huang had a third affair with an additional, unnamed employee of Nvidia.

Nvidia said its board had accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress , will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.

Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.

Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26.

“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”

The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed.

After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.

Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.

The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.

According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.

items.title: Microsoft’s global outage may be worse than Amazon's or CrowdStrike's, expert says
items.summary: Governments, hospitals, courts scrambled by global Microsoft outage.
items.content:
A global outage taking down a wide range of Microsoft 365 services remains ongoing Friday morning.

The outage started midday Thursday, impacting users of Microsoft email, cloud, and AI services. Microsoft has documented the full list of services impacted by the error, while moving early Friday morning to protect customers around the world from losing emails during the extended disruptions.

“Recovery actions are ongoing,” the Microsoft 365 Status account confirmed on X. “To help preserve delayed mail during this event, we’ve extended email timeout to 48 hours.”

Similar to recent world-shaking outages of widely used tech like Amazon Web Services and CrowdStrike , the Microsoft disruption looks like “one of the biggest outages of all time,” Ciaran Martin, the former head of the UK’s National Cyber Security Centre, told NBC News . Possibly even “worse,” he suggested.

Businesses, hospitals, police departments, and schools were among those scrambling to work around the outage. In Japan, it disrupted government IT infrastructure, according to deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki. NBC’s report documented various harms, noting that “few public bodies were immune from the outage.” In some cases, doctors couldn’t send patients “important” updates on medication changes or follow-up care.

The financial sector suffered, too, with people blocked from making bank transfers since they couldn’t receive verification codes.

Justice systems were also hobbled. The Supreme Court in the Philippines saw its legal work derailed, NBC reported. And one US sheriff’s office in Colorado reported that the outage made it difficult for people to post bond for prisoners’ immediate release.

It’s unclear how many users were affected, but Microsoft estimated in January that the total number of paid Microsoft 365 commercial subscriptions exceeded 450 million.

On a status page, Microsoft said “we have no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident” and promised to “share a full Post-Incident Report with root cause and defense-in-depth actions after mitigation is complete.”

“We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” Microsoft said on X.

But Microsoft’s public statements make clear that the tech giant was blindsided by the outage and struggled for hours to find mitigations that could reliably restore user access.

Shortly after detecting the outage, Microsoft confirmed that the main issue was “a portion of infrastructure” that “is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions.” This was not caused by increased traffic, Microsoft said, but “a problem that’s causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable.”

Once it became clear that the failed health checks were to blame, Microsoft said it took steps to prevent additional server outages while validating alternate health check methods. But four hours later, the company admitted that it was still in the weeds.

“We’re opening all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief,” Microsoft said. “We found a core process on affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, causing capacity loss. To validate a potential recovery, we’re isolating a portion of infrastructure, restarting affected components, and reintroducing traffic to confirm the services remain stable before applying the change more broadly.”

Even small wins seemed to turn into new setbacks. As Microsoft worked to resolve the issue, some of the servers it brought back online would “become unresponsive again once they receive traffic,” giving the company yet another problem to solve.

Realizing that no quick solutions were coming, Microsoft moved to extend email timeout to 48 hours. As “encouraging” recovery efforts remained ongoing, Microsoft advised users that “some intermittent issues may continue” when traffic is restored.

Microsoft’s most recent updates confirmed that it’s seeing “broader improvements in North America, sustained improvements across much of Europe, and encouraging recovery signals in Asia Pacific.”

“Some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as mitigation continues across remaining affected infrastructure,” Microsoft said. “Our focus remains on stabilizing recovered infrastructure, completing mitigation in remaining impacted areas, and reducing delayed email queues and backlogs while we validate service consistency across connection methods.”

DownDetector, which tracks user reports of service issues globally, showed that connectivity losses peaked Thursday afternoon and dropped off substantially by Friday morning.

In comments, an Outlook user described the pain of monitoring email recovery, complaining that outgoing messages seem to send fine but incoming messages are received inconsistently. Some Copilot users seemed distressed that access wasn’t restored as quickly as Outlook. One Microsoft 365 user pondered , “How many offices had people with practically nothing to do? How much has this cost?”
